claim: CRISPR-Cas9 is a molecular tool with transformative genome editing capabilities.
source: CRISPR-Cas9 (clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeat and associated Cas9 protein) is a molecular tool with transformative genome editing capabilities.
evidence: This is a general statement about CRISPR-Cas9 capabilities, supported by established scientific knowledge in the field.

claim: An intricate allosteric signaling is critical for DNA cleavage in CRISPR-Cas9.
source: At the molecular level, an intricate allosteric signaling is critical for DNA cleavage, but its role in the specificity enhancement of the Cas9 endonuclease is poorly understood.
evidence: This claim is supported by the study's investigation combining MD simulations, NMR, and graph theory to probe allosteric signaling.

claim: The role of allosteric signaling in the specificity enhancement of Cas9 is poorly understood.
source: At the molecular level, an intricate allosteric signaling is critical for DNA cleavage, but its role in the specificity enhancement of the Cas9 endonuclease is poorly understood.
evidence: This statement identifies a knowledge gap that the study aims to address.

claim: Mutations responsible for increasing the specificity of Cas9 alter the allosteric structure of the catalytic HNH domain.
source: We show that mutations responsible for increasing the specificity of Cas9 alter the allosteric structure of the catalytic HNH domain, impacting the signal transmission from the DNA recognition region to the catalytic sites for cleavage.
evidence: This claim is supported by multi-microsecond MD simulations, solution NMR data, and graph theory-derived models presented in the manuscript.

claim: The K855A mutation strongly disrupts the allosteric connectivity of the HNH domain.
source: Specifically, the K855A mutation strongly disrupts the allosteric connectivity of the HNH domain, exerting the highest perturbation on the signaling transfer, while K810A and K848A result in more moderate effects on the allosteric communication.
evidence: This is supported by computational analysis of edge betweenness changes and NMR chemical shift perturbations shown in the figures.

claim: K810A and K848A result in more moderate effects on the allosteric communication compared to K855A.
source: Specifically, the K855A mutation strongly disrupts the allosteric connectivity of the HNH domain, exerting the highest perturbation on the signaling transfer, while K810A and K848A result in more moderate effects on the allosteric communication.
evidence: This comparative claim is supported by the differential perturbation analysis shown in Figures 2 and 4.

claim: The differential perturbation of the allosteric signal correlates to the order of specificity enhancement (K855A > K848A ~ K810A) observed in biochemical studies.
source: This differential perturbation of the allosteric signal correlates to the order of specificity enhancement (K855A > K848A ~ K810A) observed in biochemical studies, with the mutation achieving the highest specificity most strongly perturbing the signaling transfer.
evidence: This correlation is inferred from comparing the biophysical data from this study with previously published biochemical data.

claim: Alterations of the allosteric communication from DNA recognition to cleavage are critical to increasing the specificity of Cas9.
source: These findings suggest that alterations of the allosteric communication from DNA recognition to cleavage are critical to increasing the specificity of Cas9 and that allosteric hotspots can be targeted through mutational studies for improving the system's function.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental and computational data showing correlation between allosteric perturbation and specificity enhancement.

claim: Allosteric hotspots can be targeted through mutational studies for improving Cas9 function.
source: These findings suggest that alterations of the allosteric communication from DNA recognition to cleavage are critical to increasing the specificity of Cas9 and that allosteric hotspots can be targeted through mutational studies for improving the system's function.
evidence: This is a speculative suggestion based on the identification of allosteric hotspots (A1-A2 communities) in the study.

claim: Cas9 can be programmed with single-guide RNAs to site-specifically recognize and cleave any desired DNA sequence.
source: At the core of the CRISPR technology, the Cas9 endonuclease can be programmed with single-guide RNAs to site-specifically recognize and cleave any desired DNA sequence, enabling easy manipulation of the genome and playing a pivotal role in gene editing applications (Jinek et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Jinek et al., 2012, a foundational paper in CRISPR technology.

claim: The RNA-programmable Cas9 generates double-stranded breaks in DNA using two endonuclease domains, HNH and RuvC.
source: The RNA-programmable Cas9 generates double-stranded breaks in DNA by first binding complementary DNA sequences and then using two endonuclease domains, HNH and RuvC.
evidence: This is established knowledge about Cas9 mechanism, supported by structural studies.

claim: A large recognition lobe (REC) mediates nucleic acid binding through three regions (REC1–3) in SpCas9.
source: Structures of Streptococcus pyogenes Cas9 (SpCas9) revealed that a large recognition lobe (REC) mediates the nucleic acid binding through three regions (REC1–3), while the spatially distinct HNH and RuvC nucleases act as molecular scissors on the two DNA strands (Figure 1; Jiang and Doudna, 2017).
evidence: This structural information is supported by citation to Jiang and Doudna, 2017, and illustrated in Figure 1.

claim: The molecular function of CRISPR-Cas9 is driven by an intricate allosteric communication critical for transferring DNA binding information from the REC lobe to the catalytic sites.
source: Biophysical studies revealed that the molecular function of CRISPR-Cas9 is driven by an intricate allosteric communication, which is critical for transferring DNA binding information from the REC lobe to the catalytic sites for cleavage (Sternberg et al., 2015 ; Chen et al., 2017; Dagdas et al., 2017; Palermo et al., 2017; Palermo et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to biophysical studies.

claim: The catalytic HNH domain is the core of the allosteric relay in Cas9.
source: Biochemical and single-molecule experiments suggested that the catalytic HNH domain is the core of this allosteric relay (Sternberg et al., 2015; Chen et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to biochemical and single-molecule experiments.

claim: The high flexibility of HNH can facilitate signal transduction.
source: Indeed, the high flexibility of HNH can facilitate the signal transduction (Jiang et al., 2016; Palermo et al., 2016), exerting conformational control over double-stranded DNA cleavage (Sternberg et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to structural and computational studies.

claim: Solution NMR and all-atom molecular dynamics indicated a dynamic pathway of allosteric residues through HNH.
source: Solution NMR and all-atom molecular dynamics (MD) indicated a dynamic pathway of allosteric residues through HNH, depicting a mechanism for biological information transfer (East et al., 2020a).
evidence: This is supported by citation to East et al., 2020a, which is a previous study by the authors.

claim: The contiguous dynamic network traverses the HNH domain, propagating the DNA binding signal from the REC region to the nucleases for concerted DNA cleavage.
source: The contiguous dynamic network traverses the HNH domain, propagating the DNA binding signal from the REC region to the nucleases (HNH and RuvC, Figure 1, left panel) for concerted DNA cleavage (Sternberg et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citation and illustrated in Figure 1.

claim: The REC-HNH-RuvC allosteric communication is critical for the system's specificity.
source: This REC-HNH-RuvC allosteric communication is also critical for the system's specificity.
evidence: This is supported by subsequent statements about off-target DNA binding affecting HNH dynamics.

claim: The binding of off-target DNA sequences at the REC lobe alters the dynamics of HNH and affects the DNA cleavage capability of Cas9.
source: Indeed, the binding of off-target DNA sequences at the REC lobe alters the dynamics of HNH and, in turn, affects the DNA cleavage capability of Cas9 (Chen et al., 2017; Dagdas et al., 2017; Ricci et al., 2019; Mitchell et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to experimental and computational studies.

claim: Three lysine-to-alanine point mutations (K810A, K848A, and K855A) within the HNH domain have shown to be important for specificity enhancement.
source: Three lysine-to-alanine (K-to-A) point mutations (i.e., K810A, K848A, and K855A) within the HNH domain have shown to be important for specificity enhancement (Slaymaker et al., 2016), but their mode of action has remained unclear.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Slaymaker et al., 2016.

claim: The mode of action of K810A, K848A, and K855A mutations has remained unclear.
source: Three lysine-to-alanine (K-to-A) point mutations (i.e., K810A, K848A, and K855A) within the HNH domain have shown to be important for specificity enhancement (Slaymaker et al., 2016), but their mode of action has remained unclear.
evidence: This identifies a knowledge gap that the current study addresses.

claim: The overall structure of HNH is maintained in the K810A, K848A, and K855A mutants.
source: The overall structure of HNH is maintained in the mutants, as also confirmed by circular dichroism analysis revealing that all systems are >95% folded at the temperature of the experiments (25°C, Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by circular dichroism data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: All K-to-A mutant systems are >95% folded at 25°C.
source: The overall structure of HNH is maintained in the mutants, as also confirmed by circular dichroism analysis revealing that all systems are >95% folded at the temperature of the experiments (25°C, Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is directly measured by circular dichroism experiments shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: K855A displays severe exchange broadening throughout the core of HNH.
source: In detail, K855A displays severe exchange broadening (where the signal-to-noise has decreased by over 20-fold, Figure 2A, gray vertical bars) throughout the core of HNH (residues 842, 848, 849, 851, and 858, Figure 2B) and many significant Δδ on the RuvC-adjacent interface (residues 780, 813, 821–828, 838–841, 850, 853, 856–872, and 903–908).
evidence: This is observed in NMR data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: K855A causes significant chemical shift perturbations on the RuvC-adjacent interface.
source: In detail, K855A displays severe exchange broadening (where the signal-to-noise has decreased by over 20-fold, Figure 2A, gray vertical bars) throughout the core of HNH (residues 842, 848, 849, 851, and 858, Figure 2B) and many significant Δδ on the RuvC-adjacent interface (residues 780, 813, 821–828, 838–841, 850, 853, 856–872, and 903–908).
evidence: This is observed in NMR chemical shift data shown in Figure 2.

claim: The regions affected by K855A are an integral part of the previously identified HNH allosteric pathway.
source: These regions are an integral part of the previously identified HNH allosteric pathway (Figure 2B; East et al., 2020a).
evidence: This is supported by comparison with the previously identified pathway shown in Figure 2B and cited from East et al., 2020a.

claim: K810A decreases the chemical shift perturbation compared to K855A.
source: K810A decreases the Δδ perturbation (residues 812–813, 834, 840–846, and 856), while K848A causes very modest chemical shift effects (residues 849 and 896).
evidence: This is observed in NMR chemical shift data shown in Figure 2.

claim: K848A causes very modest chemical shift effects.
source: K810A decreases the Δδ perturbation (residues 812–813, 834, 840–846, and 856), while K848A causes very modest chemical shift effects (residues 849 and 896).
evidence: This is observed in NMR chemical shift data shown in Figure 2.

claim: The overall degree of chemical shift perturbation decreases from K855A > K810A > K848A.
source: Most notably, the overall degree of Δδ perturbation decreases from K855A > K810A > K848A (Figure 2C, black bars).
evidence: This trend is shown in the total chemical shift data in Figure 2C.

claim: K855A is fully embedded in the allosteric pathway and shows the largest chemical shift perturbation.
source: Indeed, K855A, which is fully embedded in the allosteric pathway, shows the largest Δδ perturbation.
evidence: This is observed from the NMR data and the location of K855A in the allosteric pathway shown in Figure 1.

claim: K810A is on the periphery of the allosteric pathway.
source: K810A, on the periphery of the pathway, decreases the Δδ perturbation, while K848A, distant from the pathway, causes more moderate chemical shift effects.
evidence: This is based on the structural location of K810A relative to the allosteric pathway shown in Figure 1.

claim: K848A is distant from the allosteric pathway.
source: K810A, on the periphery of the pathway, decreases the Δδ perturbation, while K848A, distant from the pathway, causes more moderate chemical shift effects.
evidence: This is based on the structural location of K848A relative to the allosteric pathway shown in Figure 1.

claim: The EP scores computed for the isolated HNH domain follow the experimental trend of the NMR chemical shift perturbations.
source: We observe that the EP scores computed for the isolated HNH domain follow the experimental trend of the NMR Δδ in the HNH construct (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is shown by comparing the EP scores (green line) with NMR data (black bars) in Figure 2A.

claim: The environmental perturbations computed for the HNH domain within full-length Cas9 are consistent with the EP scores of the isolated HNH domain.
source: It is also notable that the environmental perturbations computed for the HNH domain within full-length Cas9 are consistent with the EP scores of the HNH domain in its isolated form (Figure 2).
evidence: This is shown by comparing data from full-length Cas9 simulations with isolated HNH simulations in Figure 2.

claim: The total environmental perturbation from MD simulations follows the experimental trend of the NMR chemical shift perturbations.
source: Overall, we observe that the total environmental perturbation arising from MD simulations follows the experimental trend of the NMR Δδ, revealing that the structural perturbation is higher in K855A and decreases in K810A and K848A (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2C comparing total chemical shift and EP scores.

claim: The structural ensemble obtained through all-atom MD properly represents the local environment determined through NMR chemical shift perturbations.
source: The qualitative agreement between the NMR Δδ and computed EP scores indicates that the structural ensemble obtained through all-atom MD for both the full-length Cas9 and the isolated HNH properly represents the local environment determined through the NMR Δδ.
evidence: This is inferred from the agreement between NMR and MD data shown in Figure 2.

claim: CPMG experiments on the three variants detected μs-ms motions in numerous residues comprising the WT pathway.
source: CPMG experiments on the three variants detected μs-ms motions in numerous residues comprising the WT pathway (e.g., G790, L791, I795, I841, F846, V856, S872, E873, I892, Q894, L900, Figure 3—figure supplement 1), with slight differences occurring in each of the variants (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is shown by CPMG relaxation dispersion data in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: The trend of curved dispersion profiles is consistent between WT HNH and the variants.
source: The trend of curved dispersion profiles is consistent between WT HNH and the variants, suggesting the retention of dynamic residues comprising the allosteric pathway in the WT Cas9 (East et al., 2020a) with modest variations in the amplitude of the curves.
evidence: This is observed from CPMG data shown in Figure 3 and Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Specificity-enhancing mutations skew the distribution of kex toward slower regimes.
source: An analysis of exchange rates, kex, derived from CPMG experiments show that specificity-enhancing mutations skew the distribution of kex toward slower regimes (Figure 3—figure supplement 3), while modestly reducing the average kex for HNH overall.
evidence: This is shown in the kex distribution data in Figure 3—figure supplement 3.

claim: The average kex for WT HNH is ~1750 s–1.
source: The <kex> for WT HNH is ~1750 s–1 (East et al., 2020a), while the mutants display similar<kex> of 1507 s–1 (K810A), 1640 s–1 (K848A), and 1580 s–1 (K855A).
evidence: This is measured from CPMG relaxation dispersion experiments, with WT data cited from East et al., 2020a.

claim: Faster (ps-ns) timescale motions are only locally altered by the mutations.
source: Likewise, faster (ps-ns) timescale motions are only locally altered by the mutations (Figure 3B and C), with good agreement between order parameters derived from WT HNH and all variants (ΔS2 ≤0.1, Figure 3—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is shown by R1R2 and NOE data in Figure 3B and C, and order parameter comparisons in Figure 3—figure supplement 4.

claim: There is good agreement between order parameters (S2) determined experimentally and computationally.
source: There is also agreement between S2 determined experimentally and computationally, consistent with 1H-[15N] NOEs that show depressed values sporadically between residues 800 and 825, surrounding residue 850, and at the C-terminus.
evidence: This is shown by comparing experimental and computational S2 values in Figure 3—figure supplement 4.

claim: The residues composing the dynamic pathways of the three variants differ very little from the WT.
source: We found that the residues composing the dynamic pathways of the three variants differ very little from the WT, and are consistent between full-length CRISPR-Cas9 and the HNH construct ( Appendix 1—figures 1–4).
evidence: This is shown by pathway analysis in Appendix 1—figures 1–4.

claim: Dynamic allosteric signaling is preserved in the Cas9 mutants.
source: This indicates that dynamic allosteric signaling is preserved in the Cas9 mutants, in agreement with CPMG relaxation experiments.
evidence: This is inferred from the pathway analysis and CPMG data showing retention of dynamics.

claim: Community network analysis identified seven communities in WT HNH.
source: First, community network analysis performed on the WT HNH identified seven communities (Figure 4A and Appendix 1—figure 5).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4A and Appendix 1—figure 5.

claim: Three communities (A1, A2, A3) hold most of the residues that display slow timescale dynamics from CPMG relaxation dispersion and compose the allosteric pathway in WT Cas9.
source: Three communities hold most of the residues that display slow timescale dynamics from CPMG relaxation dispersion, and that compose the allosteric pathway in the WT Cas9 (East et al., 2020a). These 'allosteric' communities (A1, yellow; A2, cyan; and A3, purple) are part of the allosteric route communicating the RuvC and REC2 interfaces (at the A1 and A3 communities, respectively).
evidence: This is shown by community network analysis in Figure 4A and comparison with CPMG data.

claim: For all mutants, there is a dramatic loss of communication between the A1 and A2 allosteric communities.
source: For all mutants, we observe a dramatic loss of communication between the A1 and A2 allosteric communities, which are central to the allosteric pathway (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is shown by the ΔEB analysis in Figure 4B showing negative (red) values between A1 and A2.

claim: The K-to-A mutations disrupt the allosteric crosstalk between RuvC and REC2.
source: This loss of communication at the core of the HNH allosteric structure indicates that the substitutions that enhance the specificity of Cas9 disrupt the allosteric crosstalk between RuvC and REC2.
evidence: This is inferred from the loss of communication between A1 and A2 communities shown in Figure 4B.

claim: An increase in specificity induced by the K-to-A mutations is associated with alteration of the HNH allosteric signaling.
source: This evidence links the enhancement of specificity to the disruption of the allosteric pathway, pinpointing that an increase in specificity induced by the K-to-A mutations is associated with alteration of the HNH allosteric signaling.
evidence: This is inferred from the correlation between allosteric disruption and known specificity enhancement.

claim: K855A mainly disrupts the crosstalk between the allosteric communities.
source: Indeed, K855A mainly disrupts the crosstalk between the allosteric communities, while the non-allosteric sites gain communication.
evidence: This is shown by the ΔEB analysis in Figure 4B.

claim: K810A and K848A display a progressive gain in communication between both allosteric and non-allosteric sites.
source: The two other mutants, K810A and K848A, display a progressive gain in communication between both allosteric and non-allosteric sites.
evidence: This is shown by the ΔEB analysis in Figure 4B showing blue (gain) connections.

claim: In K810A and K848A mutants, the allosteric A1 and A2 communities gain communication with the non-allosteric NA1 and NA2 regions.
source: In these mutants, the allosteric A1 and A2 communities gain communication with the non-allosteric NA1 and NA2 regions.
evidence: This is shown by the ΔEB analysis in Figure 4B.

claim: There is a decrease in the dynamic exchange between the allosteric communities upon mutation.
source: From this analysis of the NMR data, we detect a decrease in the dynamic exchange between the allosteric communities upon mutation (represented by thinner bonds compared to the WT), while an increase is observed with the non-allosteric communities.
evidence: This is shown in the community network analysis of NMR CPMG data in Figure 5.

claim: The reduction of dynamic exchange between allosteric communities and greater involvement of non-allosteric communities in the mutants is consistent with the mutation-induced EB determined from computational analysis.
source: Overall, the reduction of dynamic exchange between allosteric communities and greater involvement of non-allosteric communities in the mutants is consistent with the mutation-induced EB determined from computational analysis (Figure 4).
evidence: This is shown by comparing NMR-based community analysis (Figure 5) with computational ΔEB analysis (Figure 4).

claim: K855A exerts the most pronounced perturbation of the signal transfer among the three mutations.
source: In summary, our results show that three K-to-A mutations alter the HNH allosteric structure, with K855A exerting the most pronounced perturbation of the signal transfer by several metrics.
evidence: This is supported by multiple lines of evidence including NMR chemical shifts, EP scores, and ΔEB analysis.

claim: The HNH domain is the crux of allosteric regulation in CRISPR-Cas9.
source: Biochemical (Sternberg et al., 2015), structural (Jiang et al., 2016), and biophysical (Chen et al., 2017; Dagdas et al., 2017; Palermo et al., 2017; Palermo et al., 2018) approaches have shown that the HNH domain is the crux of this allosteric regulation, possessing a striking flexibility that facilitates the signal transduction (Jiang et al., 2016; Palermo et al., 2016) and controls DNA cleavage (Sternberg et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to biochemical, structural, and biophysical studies.

claim: K855A induces the most significant structural perturbations among the three mutations.
source: The NMR Δδ revealed that K855A induces the most significant structural perturbations, while K810A and K848A progressively reveal weakened perturbations (Figure 2).
evidence: This is shown by NMR chemical shift data in Figure 2.

claim: The three mutants retain the overall dynamic pathway responsible for information transfer.
source: We found that the three mutants retain the overall dynamic pathway responsible for information transfer, indicating that the allosteric signaling is preserved (Figure 3 and Appendix 1—figure 4).
evidence: This is shown by pathway analysis in Figure 3 and Appendix 1—figure 4.

claim: The K-to-A mutations disrupt the main communication channel between RuvC and REC.
source: In-depth analysis of the community network (Figure 4) revealed that the K-to-A mutations disrupt the main communication channel between RuvC and REC, as evidenced by a decrease in the mutation-induced edge betweennesses difference (ΔEB) between the allosteric communities A1–A3 that are central to the pathway (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is shown by ΔEB analysis in Figure 4B.

claim: The K-to-A mutations consistently disrupt the crosstalk between allosteric sites A1 and A2.
source: Interestingly, computational and experimental data indicate that the K-to-A mutations consistently disrupt the crosstalk between allosteric sites A1 and A2 (Figure 4), suggesting that these communities could be critical allosteric hotspots for the signal transmission (Figure 6).
evidence: This is shown by both computational ΔEB analysis and NMR-based community analysis in Figures 4 and 5.

claim: The A1–A2 communities could be critical allosteric hotspots for signal transmission.
source: Interestingly, computational and experimental data indicate that the K-to-A mutations consistently disrupt the crosstalk between allosteric sites A1 and A2 (Figure 4), suggesting that these communities could be critical allosteric hotspots for the signal transmission (Figure 6).
evidence: This is inferred from the consistent disruption of A1-A2 communication across all mutants.

claim: Future mutational studies of residues comprising the A1–A2 communities could impact the allosteric communication and modulate the function and specificity of Cas9.
source: Building on this observation, future mutational studies of residues comprising the A1–A2 communities (i.e., residues 839–856, 864–869, 809–828, and 857–863) could impact the allosteric communication and, in turn, modulate the function and specificity of the system.
evidence: This is a speculative suggestion based on the identification of A1-A2 as allosteric hotspots.

claim: K855A more strongly disrupts the communication between allosteric sites compared to K848A and K810A.
source: In-depth analysis of the computational data also reveals that K855A more strongly disrupts the communication between allosteric sites, compared to K848A and K810A that display a lesser impact (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is shown by the ΔEB analysis in Figure 4B.

claim: Among the three K-to-A mutations, K855A has shown to achieve the highest specificity enhancement as a single point mutation.
source: Interestingly, among the three K-to-A mutations, K855A has shown to achieve the highest specificity enhancement as a single point mutation (Slaymaker et al., 2016).
evidence: This is cited from Slaymaker et al., 2016.

claim: The specificity enhancement of the three single mutants toward the off-target validating VEGFA gene follows the K855A > K848A ~ K810A order.
source: Indeed, the specificity enhancement of the three single mutants toward the off-target validating VEGFA gene follows the K855A > K848A ~ K810A order.
evidence: This is cited from Slaymaker et al., 2016.

claim: K810A and K848A required further optimization to achieve maximal specificity.
source: In the same study, K810A and K848A required further optimization to achieve maximal specificity.
evidence: This is cited from Slaymaker et al., 2016.

claim: The biophysical aspects of allosteric signal perturbation mirror the biochemistry of specificity enhancement in the three single point mutants.
source: Hence, the biophysical aspects of allosteric signal perturbation mirror the biochemistry of specificity enhancement in these three single point mutants.
evidence: This is inferred from the correlation between the magnitude of allosteric perturbation and the order of specificity enhancement.

claim: K855A could most prominently leverage the HNH allosterism to improve the system's specificity.
source: On the basis of these observations, K855A, which strongly impacts allosteric communication, could most prominently leverage the HNH allosterism to improve the system's specificity.
evidence: This is inferred from the strong allosteric perturbation caused by K855A and its high specificity enhancement.

claim: The HNH allosteric signal is critical for transferring DNA binding information from the REC region to the catalytic sites of HNH and RuvC.
source: The HNH allosteric signal is indeed critical for transferring DNA binding information from the REC region to the catalytic sites of HNH and RuvC, and is a cornerstone of CRISPR-Cas9 specificity.
evidence: This is supported by citations to single-molecule, kinetic, and computational studies.

claim: Single-molecule and kinetic experiments have shown that the binding of off-target DNA sequences at REC affects the dynamics of HNH and its allosteric activation of DNA cleavage.
source: Single-molecule and kinetic experiments (Chen et al., 2017; Dagdas et al., 2017), as well as computational analysis (Palermo et al., 2018; Ricci et al., 2019; Mitchell et al., 2020), have shown that the binding of off-target DNA sequences at REC affects the dynamics of HNH and its allosteric activation of DNA cleavage.
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to experimental and computational studies.

claim: Three specificity-enhancing mutations disrupt the HNH signaling mechanism.
source: Our investigations show that three specificity-enhancing mutations disrupt this signaling mechanism.
evidence: This is shown by the ΔEB analysis and NMR data demonstrating loss of communication between allosteric communities.

claim: The magnitude of change in allosteric communication correlates to the biochemical trends in specificity enhancement (K855A > K848A ~ K810A).
source: Considering that the magnitude of change in allosteric communication correlates to the biochemical trends in specificity enhancement (K855A > K848A ~ K810A) (East et al., 2020a), the structural and dynamic perturbations caused by K-to-A mutants can be related to the enzyme's increased specificity.
evidence: This correlation is inferred from comparing the biophysical data with biochemical specificity data.

claim: The structural and dynamic perturbations caused by K-to-A mutants can be related to the enzyme's increased specificity.
source: Considering that the magnitude of change in allosteric communication correlates to the biochemical trends in specificity enhancement (K855A > K848A ~ K810A) (East et al., 2020a), the structural and dynamic perturbations caused by K-to-A mutants can be related to the enzyme's increased specificity.
evidence: This is inferred from the correlation between allosteric perturbation and specificity enhancement.

claim: K810A and K848A mutants require additional substitutions to achieve maximal specificity.
source: The K810A and K848A mutants, which affect the HNH structure and dynamics in a more moderate way, could exert a lower allosteric effect on the specificity enhancement. As noted above, these mutants require additional substitutions to achieve maximal specificity (Slaymaker et al., 2016).
evidence: This is cited from Slaymaker et al., 2016.

claim: The additional K1003A and R1060A mutations are localized away from HNH.
source: The additional K1003A and R1060A mutations localized away from HNH (Figure 7) and might exploit different mechanisms to improve Cas9 specificity, such as altering the interactions with the distal bases of the DNA non-target strand (Slaymaker et al., 2016).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 7 and cited from Slaymaker et al., 2016.

claim: The K1003A and R1060A mutations might exploit different mechanisms to improve Cas9 specificity, such as altering the interactions with the distal bases of the DNA non-target strand.
source: The additional K1003A and R1060A mutations localized away from HNH (Figure 7) and might exploit different mechanisms to improve Cas9 specificity, such as altering the interactions with the distal bases of the DNA non-target strand (Slaymaker et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a hypothesis cited from Slaymaker et al., 2016.

claim: The K1003A and R1060A mutations induce a remarkable flexibility of the distal DNA bases, compared to the WT Cas9.
source: The K1003A and R1060A mutations induce a remarkable flexibility of the distal DNA bases, compared to the WT Cas9 (Figure 7), consistent with the hypothesis that the specificity enhancement of these mutants could also arise from the neutralization of positive charges interacting at the level of the DNA non-target strand (Slaymaker et al., 2016).
evidence: This is shown by MD simulations of triple mutants in Figure 7.

claim: The neutralization of positive charges at the DNA non-target strand could favor the re-hybridization of DNA in the presence of off-target sequences, thereby limiting off-target cleavage.
source: This could indeed favor the re-hybridization of DNA in the presence of off-target sequences, thereby limiting off-target cleavage (Singh et al., 2016 ; Singh et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a mechanistic hypothesis supported by citations to Singh et al., 2016 and 2018.

claim: K855A could increase specificity by mainly leveraging the HNH allosterism.
source: Taken together, our observations suggest that K855A could increase the specificity by mainly leveraging the HNH allosterism, while K810A and K848A could combine more moderate allosteric effects with the weakening of the interactions at the DNA non-target strand.
evidence: This is inferred from the strong allosteric effects of K855A and the additional mutations required for K810A and K848A.

claim: K810A and K848A could combine more moderate allosteric effects with the weakening of the interactions at the DNA non-target strand.
source: Taken together, our observations suggest that K855A could increase the specificity by mainly leveraging the HNH allosterism, while K810A and K848A could combine more moderate allosteric effects with the weakening of the interactions at the DNA non-target strand.
evidence: This is inferred from the moderate allosteric effects of K810A and K848A and the need for additional mutations.

claim: The combination of allosteric and electrostatic effects could be critical for the triple mutants optimized for both specificity and activity.
source: This combination of allosteric and electrostatic effects could be critical for the triple mutants, which were optimized for both specificity and activity, with eSpCas9 1.1 being widely used in vitro (Slaymaker et al., 2016).
evidence: This is inferred from the analysis of both allosteric and electrostatic mechanisms.

claim: In addition to electrostatic effects, the K-to-A mutants alter HNH dynamics, impacting the allosteric communication between REC and RuvC.
source: Our investigations show that, in addition to electrostatic effects, the K-to-A mutants alter HNH dynamics, impacting the allosteric communication between REC and RuvC (Sternberg et al., 2015; Chen et al., 2017; Dagdas et al., 2017; Palermo et al., 2017; Palermo et al., 2018).
evidence: This is shown by the ΔEB analysis and NMR data in the study.

claim: The altered allosteric communication has a profound influence on Cas9 activation, representing an important source for the observed specificity enhancement.
source: This altered communication has a profound influence on Cas9 activation, representing an important source for the observed specificity enhancement.
evidence: This is inferred from the correlation between allosteric perturbation and specificity enhancement.

claim: The allosteric crosstalk can be targeted for improving the system's specificity.
source: We therefore suggest that the allosteric crosstalk can be targeted for improving the system's specificity, as reported for other allosteric proteins (Liu and Nussinov, 2016).
evidence: This is a suggestion based on the findings and supported by citation to Liu and Nussinov, 2016.

claim: The critical hotspots identified (A1-A2 communities) offer novel insight for mutational studies of CRISPR-Cas9 aimed at further controlling its function.
source: In this respect, the critical hotspots identified here (Figure 6) offer novel insight for mutational studies of CRISPR-Cas9, aimed at further controlling its function.
evidence: This is a suggestion based on the identification of A1-A2 as allosteric hotspots.

claim: The combination of solution NMR and molecular simulations enabled translation of the allosteric signaling from the individual HNH domain to full-length Cas9 with atomic level detail.
source: Finally, it is worth noting that the combination of solution NMR and molecular simulations enabled us to translate the allosteric signaling from the individual HNH domain to full-length Cas9 with atomic level detail.
evidence: This describes the methodological approach used in the study.

claim: The 'bottom-up' approach exploits the capability of solution NMR to identify allosteric motions within optimized constructs of the multi-domain Cas9 protein while all-atom MD simulations characterize the communication network within the full-length Cas9.
source: This 'bottom-up' approach exploits the capability of solution NMR to identify allosteric motions within optimized constructs of the multi-domain Cas9 protein (East et al., 2020a; Nerli et al., 2021), while all-atom MD simulations are used to characterize the communication network within the full-length Cas9.
evidence: This describes the methodological strategy of the study.

claim: The X-ray structure of the HNH construct displays a root mean square deviation (RMSD) difference for the Cα below 1 Å (0.92 Å) when compared to the structure of HNH crystallized within full-length Cas9.
source: The structure of the HNH domain (residues 775–908) crystallized within the full-length Cas9 (PDB: 5F9R, green) (Jiang and Doudna, 2017) is superposed on the X-ray structure of the HNH construct (PDB: 6O56, blue).(East et al., 2020a). The two structures display a root mean square deviation (RMSD) difference for the C⍺ below 1 Å (i.e., 0.92 Å).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: K855A and K810A have lower melting points (46.5°C and 51.4°C respectively) than K848A (60.6°C) and the WT (56.6°C).
source: K855A (46.5°C) and K810A (51.4°C) have a lower melting point than K848A (60.6°C) and the WT (56.6°C).
evidence: This is measured by CD melting curves shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2B.

claim: All HNH systems are >95% folded at 25°C.
source: Importantly, all systems are >95% folded at the temperature of the experiments (25°C).
evidence: This is determined from CD melting curves shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2B.

claim: Multi-microsecond molecular dynamics simulations were combined with solution NMR and graph theory-derived models to probe the allosteric role of key specificity-enhancing mutations.
source: Here, multi-microsecond molecular dynamics is combined with solution NMR and graph theory-derived models to probe the allosteric role of key specificity-enhancing mutations.
evidence: This describes the methodological approach of the study.

claim: An ~1.2 µs-long trajectory was collected in three replicas for the WT CRISPR-Cas9 system and for each of the K845A, K855A, and H855A variants.
source: An ~1.2 µs-long trajectory was collected in three replicas for the WT CRISPR-Cas9 system and for each of the K845A, K855A, and H855A variants.
evidence: This describes the simulation protocol used in the study.

claim: A total of ~14.4 µs of MD was collected for the full-length CRISPR-Cas9 and also for the isolated HNH domain.
source: This resulted in ~3.6 µs of MD for each simulated system and a total of ~14.4 µs of MD for the full-length CRISPR-Cas9 and also for the isolated HNH domain.
evidence: This describes the total simulation time used in the study.
